answer_1.quote: We performed a study in which human subjects were presented with pairs of words of the same part of speech together with their definitions (generated by GPT-3, for fake words, or extracted from the dictionary, for rare words)...

answer_2.quote: For each word w and definition d in the lexicon... we compute the likelihood under GPT-3 of the definition d to follow word w, p(d|w)... we compute the difference in log-likelihood between the proper match... (LLD).

answer_3.quote: If GPT-3 were to perform the matching task done by our human subjects, it would choose the option with higher total likelihood. In other words, it would prefer the correct pairing if LLD(w1, w2) is negative and the inverted pairing if it is positive.

answer_4.quote: We performed a study in which human subjects were presented with pairs of words... Users were asked to decide which assignment of definitions to words is a better fit and to rate their confidence.
answer_4.guideline: Decide which definition matches each word better and rate confidence on a 0‑5 scale.
